title: Clopen lift and adjunction-normalized component projection for a proper/open square
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring. For every scheme $X$ use its small pro-etale site with the chosen small skeleton, its constant ring sheaf $\underline B_X$, the abelian category of module sheaves, and $\mathcal T_X=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline B_X))$ of strict inverse systems. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal T_X)$. Use the termwise inverse image $G_u$, total derived termwise direct image $R_u$, and exact open extension $J_j$ with their specified adjunctions and compositors [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations] [def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension]. Let $Q$ be a commutative square of schemes with $k:V\hookrightarrow W$, $i:S\hookrightarrow T$ quasi-compact open immersions, $r:V\to S$ and $p:W\to T$ proper, and $pk=ir$. Put $W_S=W\times_T S$ with projections $b:W_S\to W$, $q:W_S\to S$, and $s=(k,r):V\to W_S$. The map $s$ is an open and closed immersion, with $bs=k$, $qs=r$; no cartesian or identity-left hypothesis is required. Put $C=W_S\setminus s(V)$ and let $c:C\hookrightarrow W_S$ be the complementary open. For every module sheaf $F$, the section decomposition over a pro-etale test object $H$ is $F(H)\cong F(H\times_{W_S}s(V))\times F(H\times_{W_S}C)$. Its first-factor projection defines a unique natural map $\pi_s:F\to s_!s^{-1}F$, identity on $s(V)$ and zero on $C$. The canonical map $t_s:s_!\to s_*$, the direct-image transpose of the inverse open unit, is an isomorphism, and $(t_s s^{-1})\circ\pi_s=\eta_s$ for the direct-image unit. Thus this section projection is exactly the adjunction-defined projection of [def-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-arrows]. The statements remain true termwise on towers and complexes and in $D(\mathcal T_{W_S})$: under the open unit $G_s\pi_s=1$, whereas $G_c\pi_s=0$ with zero target. Define $\alpha_Q=(J_b\pi_sG_q)\circ\beta_{i,p}$, followed by $J_bJ_sG_sG_q\cong J_kG_r$. In a cartesian square, identify $V$ with $W_S$ by its canonical pullback isomorphism; then $s=1$ and $\alpha_Q=\beta_{i,p}$; if $V=S$, $r=1$, it is projection to the clopen section $(k,1_S)$. These are assertions about actual transformations, independent of evaluation faithfulness.

proof.text: Apply the proved clopenSections_bijective from the ringed-module gluing module to the two-element family consisting of s and c. The complement equation gives disjointness in both orders and coverage. The resulting restriction bijection is exactly the two stated clopenTestInclusion maps.

Transport the fixed-coefficient sheaf open adjunction through the module equivalences fixedRestriction. Its unit is invertible on an open immersion. For a clopen immersion the proved moduleClopenIso identifies extension by zero with direct image. Full faithfulness of extension and uniqueness of the normalized transpose show that the specified clopenModuleToDirect is invertible.

proof.text: Define the projector by the direct-image unit followed by the inverse normalized comparison, as already specified. A generic adjunction-triple calculation gives its open restriction: the comparison is counit followed by unit, and the open triangle identity cancels the counit. On the complement, disjoint open extension has zero restriction: apply the existing pro-etale isZero_upperStar_openImmersionLowerShriek theorem, transporting along fixedPull and fixedOpen, then reflect the zero object through the faithful constant-coefficient equivalence. Maps into extension are determined by open restriction, using the direct-image adjunction and its comparison isomorphism; hence uniqueness. On sections, compose evaluation of the extension/direct-image isomorphism with evaluation of the mate of fixedDirect. Its unit equation identifies the projector with ordinary restriction to the clopen test piece, giving the required additive equivalence and first-factor formula.

Whisker the ordinary natural transformation to strict towers and then to cochain complexes. Naturality gives the transition and differential equations automatically. Equality of tower morphisms and complex morphisms is componentwise equality, and their zero targets follow from the componentwise zero identity. This is all before localization.

proof.text: Use the exact tower pullback and open extension already constructed. Descend the termwise projector by Localization.liftNatTrans and transport its source and target through the exact-derived identity and composition comparisons. Their factorization equations give the required cochain representative equation. This construction uses ordinary unbounded localization and imposes no bound or finiteness assumption.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), parts (3)-(4); exact derived factorization and comparison with the right derived functor; homology.tex Tag 02MZ (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian)

proof.text: The exactAdj_unit equation from the proper/open arrows identifies the open unit on cochain representatives. Apply localization natural-transformation extensionality to descend the ordinary open-restriction equation. Independently, the adjunction-triple triangle calculation gives the same restriction equation for the intrinsic pi. Cancel the invertible open-to-direct comparison and transpose under G_s left adjoint to R_s to identify the descended map with pi on every derived object. For complementary vanishing first use the invertible ordinary open unit and the tower vanishing clause to show that the exact composite towerJ(s) followed by towerPullback(c) kills every tower. Exact derived functor homology compatibility then shows its derived composite kills every object, and the derived composition isomorphism gives the claimed zero target.

proof.text: The alpha formula is its defining equation. The cartesian pullback lift is hsq.isoPullback.hom by the pullback projection equations, hence is invertible. Its inverse image is faithful: compose with inverse image of the inverse scheme map, and use gComp and gId to identify the composite with identity. Applying that faithful functor, the projector restriction equation and the open adjunction triangle show pi_s followed by the open counit equals identity. Apply betaInv_source_factorization to s and the canonical fibre-product projections. Cancel the inverse beta on the right of the asserted alpha=beta equation, use naturality of the open compositor, cancel its inverse and the inverse-image compositor, and use the projector-counit identity. The remaining beta and inverse beta cancel. Finally qs=identity is the pullback equation, and both section restriction equations are the already proved clopenDerived_section_projector clauses.

lean.statement: theorem properOpen_clopen_projector {V W S T : Scheme.{u}} (k : V ⟶ W) (r : V ⟶ S) (p : W ⟶ T) (i : S ⟶ T) [IsOpenImmersion k] [IsOpenImmersion i] [QuasiCompact k] [QuasiCompact i] [IsProper r] [IsProper p] (h : k ≫ p = r ≫ i) : (alpha B k r p i h = (beta B (pullback.snd p i) (pullback.fst p i) i p pullback.condition.symm (IsPullback.of_hasPullback p i).flip).hom ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (Functor.whiskerLeft (G B (pullback.snd p i)) (pi B (squareLift k r p i h))) (J B (pullback.fst p i)) ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (Functor.associator (G B (pullback.snd p i)) (G B (squareLift k r p i h)) (J B (squareLift k r p i h))).inv (J B (pullback.fst p i)) ≫ (Functor.associator (G B (pullback.snd p i) ⋙ G B (squareLift k r p i h)) (J B (squareLift k r p i h)) (J B (pullback.fst p i))).hom ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft (G B (pullback.snd p i) ⋙ G B (squareLift k r p i h)) ((jComp B (squareLift k r p i h) (pullback.fst p i)).hom ≫ (jCongr B (pullback.lift_fst k r h)).hom) ≫ Functor.whiskerRight ((gComp B (squareLift k r p i h) (pullback.snd p i)).inv ≫ (eqToIso (congrArg (G B) (pullback.lift_snd k r h))).hom) (J B k)) ∧ (∀ hsq : IsPullback k r p i, IsIso (squareLift k r p i h) ∧ alpha B k r p i h = (beta B r k i p h.symm hsq.flip).hom) ∧ (∀ (k' : S ⟶ W) [IsOpenImmersion k'] [QuasiCompact k'] (h' : k' ≫ p = (𝟙 S) ≫ i), squareLift k' (𝟙 S) p i h' ≫ pullback.snd p i = 𝟙 S ∧ ∀ (C : Scheme.{u}) (c : C ⟶ pullback p i) [IsOpenImmersion c], Set.range c = (Set.range (squareLift k' (𝟙 S) p i h'))ᶜ → ∀ M : Derived B (pullback p i), (G B (squareLift k' (𝟙 S) p i h')).map ((pi B (squareLift k' (𝟙 S) p i h')).app M) = (jAdj B (squareLift k' (𝟙 S) p i h')).unit.app ((G B (squareLift k' (𝟙 S) p i h')).obj M) ∧ (G B c).map ((pi B (squareLift k' (𝟙 S) p i h')).app M) = 0)
